newsitem.title: BELGIUM: PetroFina reassures on Fina offer.
newsitem.headline: PetroFina reassures on Fina offer.

text.p: Francois Cornelis, chief executive officer of Belgian oil and gas group PetroFina, said on Monday its shareholders should not be worried by its plans to take full-control of 85.4 percent U.S. subsidiary Fina Inc.
PetroFina said in February it would offer $60 a share for the shares it does not already hold in Fina. Since then, Fina's share price has risen to $65.

"I don't want to comment on recent declarations made concerning Fina. I would just like to say that we shall not pay more than is economically justifiable and that PetroFina shareholders need not be concerned about this," Cornelis said.
PetroFina has not yet tabled a final Fina offer. An independent report valuing the U.S. company has not yet been presented, Cornelis noted.
Cornelis said, however, PetroFina hoped funds to pay for the Fina buy would come from a warrant on its own share that can be exercised at a price of 12,500 francs between May 20 and June 3.
According to the group's annual report, 1,162,611 warrants are outstanding, indicating the group could raise around 14.5 billion francs if all warrants were exercised.
A $60 offer for the outstanding Fina shares would cost PetroFina around nine billion francs.
Cornelis said no additional capital increase was planned to pay for Fina.
"The commitment the board took was that if we do issue stock for Fina we would buy back the same amount of stock from the market in order to compensate our shareholders," Cornelis said.
Cornelis said PetroFina was not behind a recent rise in the company's share price, which analysts have speculated may have been a deliberate attempt to encourage investors to exercise the warrants.
